payload.name: ExtractPlansFromInvitationReplies
payload.description: During extraction, use when a speaker replies to an invitation or question about future plans with concrete desired activities, even if tentative ('maybe we can', 'I'd love to').
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker responds to an invitation or a question about future plans by naming concrete activities they would like to do, create a plan candidate even if the message has no explicit date or commitment words.

Use 'plan' as the memory type for activities to be done together at a future visit or event; include the participants and the activity, and resolve relative times ('tomorrow', 'when I come over') from the message timestamp.
Do not skip such replies because they are conversational or tentative; 'maybe we can' or 'I'd love to' still expresses an intention worth persisting.

solves: When a speaker replies to an invitation or a question about upcoming plans by naming concrete activities they would like to do together, the Construction Agent sometimes fails to extract any candidate, so the plan is never persisted. This pattern occurs across any future-visit, meeting, or event dialogue whenever tentative or conversational phrasing still expresses a clear intention. The skill generalizes the need to treat such replies as plan candidates regardless of the specific activity, time, or participants.
